Package com.egradx.auth

Class EgradxRoleService

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.auth.EgradxRoleService
public class EgradxRoleService extends Object
Manages roles and their granular authorities, and assigns/revokes a user's role within a specific organization. A role is just a named bundle of authorities — the authorization unit an admin thinks in terms of. It is not the unit an access check is written against: resolveAuthorityNames(java.util.UUID, java.util.UUID) flattens the one role a user holds in a given organization down to the flat set of authority names it grants; that flat set — never role names — is what EgradxPermissionResolver resolves fresh on every request.

Every role belongs to exactly one organization — including the platform organization's own roles, which are ordinary roles in an ordinary organization. There is no null organization anywhere in this API any more.

Roles are addressed by id in everything an administrator drives, and by name only where a caller is seeding known roles (createSystemRole(java.util.UUID, java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.util.Set<java.lang.String>)) — a name is a natural key but a poor handle, since renaming a role would otherwise invalidate a request in flight.

    • createSystemRole

      @Transactional public EgradxRoleDto createSystemRole(UUID organizationId, String name, String description, Set<String> authorityNames)
      For seeding an organization's (or the platform's) default roles — identical to createRole(java.util.UUID, com.egradx.auth.dto.EgradxCreateRoleRequest) except the created role is marked isSystem, protecting it from deleteRole(java.util.UUID, java.util.UUID). There is no fixed catalog of default roles/authorities baked into this class — the caller decides what to seed and with which authorities.

    • replaceRolePermissions

      @Transactional public EgradxRoleDto replaceRolePermissions(UUID organizationId, UUID roleId, Set<UUID> permissionIds)
      Replaces a role's entire permission set in one shot — the operation an admin UI's "check the boxes, save" screen actually performs. An empty set strips the role back to granting nothing.
      Throws:
      NotFoundException - if the role, or any named permission, doesn't exist (an unknown id fails loudly rather than silently granting less)
      ValidationException - if a platform-only authority is being granted to a role outside the platform organization — see EgradxAuthorities.PLATFORM_ONLY

    • assignRoleToUser

      @Transactional public void assignRoleToUser(UUID userId, UUID organizationId, String roleName)
      Sets — not adds — the given role as the user's single role within organizationId, creating the membership if this is the user's first role in that organization or replacing it if they already had a different one there. A user may hold a different role in a different organization; see EgradxOrganizationMembershipEntity.
      Throws:
      NotFoundException - if the user or the role doesn't exist (the role lookup is itself organization-scoped, so a role id from a different organization can never be assigned here)

    • resolveAuthorityNames

      public Set<String> resolveAuthorityNames(UUID userId, UUID organizationId)
      The set of authority names granted by the one role a user holds in organizationId — empty, not an error, if they have no membership there.

      Not on the cached path — it calls getAuthorityNamesForRole(java.util.UUID) via this, which bypasses the @Cacheable proxy (see that method's javadoc). Fine for a one-off lookup like login, but EgradxDefaultPermissionResolver — the per-request path this exists to support — calls resolveRoleId(java.util.UUID, java.util.UUID) and getAuthorityNamesForRole(java.util.UUID) itself instead of this convenience method, specifically to stay on the cached path.

    • getAuthorityNamesForRole

      @Cacheable(cacheNames="egradx-role-authorities", key="#roleId") public Set<String> getAuthorityNamesForRole(UUID roleId)
      Split out from resolveAuthorityNames(java.util.UUID, java.util.UUID) so it can be cached per role (a role is shared by every member with that role, unlike a per-user resolution). Cache entries are evicted by EgradxRoleAuthoritiesCacheEvictionListener after the transaction that changed a role's authorities commits — see replaceRolePermissions(java.util.UUID, java.util.UUID, java.util.Set<java.util.UUID>)/addAuthoritiesToRole(java.util.UUID, java.lang.String, java.util.Set<java.lang.String>). Never call this method from elsewhere in this class — self-invocation bypasses Spring's AOP cache proxy and would silently skip caching entirely.
